source: GQL = GraphQL-Learn-Official.pdf (capture of graphql.org/learn, 6 pages, generated 2026-08-18 per metadata; no spec/library version declared)
convention: page = PDF page (1-6); the source has no printed numbering

entries.title: Learn GraphQL landing page
entries.summary: Presents the site as a tutorial-style introduction to the core concepts of every GraphQL API, in a step-by-step path from basic queries to advanced features. Says the reader will see the basics, how GraphQL compares to other technologies and then best practices for designing APIs. Lists four tabs: Learn GraphQL, Tutorials, Best Practices, FAQ.

entries.title: Lesson 1: Introduction
entries.summary: High-level overview of GraphQL and of how it enables flexible, versionless APIs backed by a strong type system. The description is cut between pages 1 and 2 in the capture; only what is written counts. The lesson content is NOT in the PDF.

entries.title: Lesson 2: Schemas and Types
entries.summary: The lesson teaches how the GraphQL schema language defines the shape of the data through types. Only the description sentence is in the PDF; the schema language syntax is not shown.

entries.title: Lesson 3: Queries
entries.summary: The lesson is about structuring queries to ask for exactly the data needed, including fields, variables and fragments. Only the description appears; no query syntax is in the PDF.

entries.title: Lesson 4: Mutations
entries.summary: The lesson is about modifying data with mutations, including updating and removing records through the schema. Only the description appears.

entries.title: Best Practices section (landing)
entries.summary: Described as practical guidelines, real-world strategies for designing and operating GraphQL APIs, to build with scale and safety. The lesson list is truncated by a 'Show more' button (lessons 1-4 visible; the rest were not captured).

entries.title: BP Lesson 1: Introduction
entries.summary: Presents the context behind the Best Practices lessons. Only the description appears.

entries.title: BP Lesson 2: Thinking In Graphs
entries.summary: Describes the mindset shift from RESTful endpoints to graph thinking, aligning the schema with business logic and legacy systems. The PDF mentions REST only in this sentence; there is no developed REST x GraphQL comparison.

entries.title: BP Lesson 3: Serving Over Http
entries.summary: Announces that the lesson explores how GraphQL operates over HTTP: methods, headers, status codes and API endpoint design. The details (which method, which statuses) are NOT in the PDF.

entries.title: BP Lesson 4: File Uploads
entries.summary: Says that file uploads are handled by wrapping them as mutations and promises the recommended approach for integrating file handling into the API. The sentence crosses the page break (pages 2-3); the approach itself is not in the PDF.

entries.title: Schema Governance section (landing)
entries.summary: States that a healthy API starts with a well-governed schema, with review processes and automated checks to keep the schema consistent, secure and easy to evolve as the team grows. There are 'Show more' and 'Explore schema governance' buttons.

entries.title: SG Lesson 1: Schema Ownership and Governance Models
entries.summary: Explores schema ownership and governance models, citing centralized, federated and hybrid approaches. Only the three names appear; no definitions.

entries.title: SG Lesson 2: Governance Tooling
entries.summary: Learn about schema governance and best practices for managing it. No tool is named.

entries.title: SG Lesson 3: Schema Review
entries.summary: Establish review processes and automated validation to keep the schema consistent, secure and easy to evolve.

entries.title: SG Lesson 4: Schema Change Management
entries.summary: Learn to manage schema changes and versioning in GraphQL, ensuring smooth evolution of the API. How (deprecation, breaking changes etc.) is NOT stated.

entries.title: Listed courses and tutorials
entries.summary: Four items, one line each: GraphQL-JS tutorial (schemas and query execution with GraphQL.js); Apollo Odyssey (interactive courses with Apollo's tools); Yoga GraphQL Server Tutorial (open source, servers in Node, CF Workers, Deno and others); Hasura GraphQL Tutorials (real-world fullstack tutorials).

entries.title: FAQ (landing)
entries.summary: Common questions, from beginners to advanced cases, including frontend concerns and information about the official specification. The page shows only six categories, with no questions or answers: Getting started, General, Best practices, Specification, Frontend, Foundation.

entries.title: Looking for more?
entries.summary: Invitation to discover tools and other resources and to connect with the GraphQL community worldwide; only two links, Resources and Community.

entries.title: Site menu and footer
entries.summary: Navigation only: LEARN (Introduction, Best Practices, FAQ, Training Courses); CODE (GitHub, Specification, Libraries & Tools, Services & Vendors); COMMUNITY (Resources, Events, Contribute, Landscape, Shop); & MORE (Blog, GraphQL Foundation, Community Grant, Brand Guidelines, Code of Conduct). entries.title: What this PDF is
entries.summary: PDF capture of graphql.org/learn (metadata title: 'Learn | GraphQL'), generated by a headless browser on 2026-08-18 (metadata), 6 pages and about 4 thousand characters. It is a lesson index and landing page: titles and one- or two-line descriptions. No lesson content, syntax, code, diagram or spec version was captured.
